sections.label: FSB OTC derivatives recommendations
sections.summary: In 2010 the FSB recommended reporting, central clearing and trading of OTC derivatives, leading to a 2012 amendment of the Securities and Futures Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In 2010, FSB introduced a set of recommendations for its members to implement reporting, central clearing and trading of over-the-counter (OTC) derivatives and to subject OTC derivatives market operators and intermediaries to stronger regulatory oversight.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Arising from the FSB's recommendations, the Securities and Futures Act (SFA) was amended in 2012, as part of this international effort to strengthen the regulation of OTC derivatives markets.

sections.label: MAS central clearing regulations
sections.summary: MAS will finalise and implement regulations for central clearing of widely traded OTC derivatives contracts later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Later this year, MAS will finalise and implement regulations for the central clearing of widely traded OTC derivatives contracts.

sections.label: MAS organised trading facility powers
sections.summary: The Bill empowers MAS to require OTC derivatives products meeting prescribed criteria to be traded on organised trading facilities such as exchanges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill also empowers MAS to require OTC derivatives products that meet prescribed criteria to be traded on organised trading facilities, such as exchanges, instead of OTC.

sections.label: MAS prescribing gold buy-back debentures
sections.summary: MAS intends to prescribe as debentures buy-back arrangements involving gold, silver and platinum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: With these powers, MAS intends to prescribe as debentures, buy-back arrangements involving gold, silver and platinum.

sections.label: Current CIS pooling requirement
sections.summary: Currently a scheme is regarded as a CIS only if both profits and contributions from investors are pooled.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Currently, for a scheme to be regarded as a CIS, both profits and contributions from investors must be pooled.

sections.label: Amended CIS pooling definition
sections.summary: The amended CIS definition will no longer require investors' contributions and profits to be pooled for a scheme to be a CIS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The amended CIS definition will no longer require investors' contributions and profits to be pooled in order for a scheme to be regarded as a CIS.

sections.label: Net personal assets calculation
sections.summary: The Bill tightens net personal assets calculation, limiting primary residence net equity to $1 million of the $2 million threshold.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill tightens the way net personal assets are calculated, such as the net equity of an individual's primary residence can only contribute up to $1 million of the $2 million threshold.

sections.label: Financial benchmarks regulatory framework
sections.summary: The Bill will introduce a new regulatory framework for financial benchmarks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill will introduce a new regulatory framework for financial benchmarks.

sections.label: MAS designating key benchmarks
sections.summary: Under the Bill, MAS can designate key financial benchmarks, and intends to designate SIBOR and the Swap Offer Rate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, MAS will be able to designate key financial benchmarks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MAS intends to designate SIBOR and the Swap Offer Rate (SOR).

sections.label: Section 199 prohibition clarified
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies that the section 199 prohibition applies regardless of the price effect.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill clarifies that the section 199 prohibition applies regardless of the price effect.

sections.label: Insider trading statutory definition
sections.summary: The new statutory definition strengthens MAS' ability to pursue insider trading cases without meeting an unrealistically high standard for persons who commonly invest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The new statutory definition will strengthen MAS' ability to pursue insider trading cases without having to meet an unrealistically high standard for "persons who commonly invest".

sections.label: Civil penalty maximum and priority
sections.summary: The Bill standardises the maximum civil penalty to the greater of $2 million or three times benefits gained or losses avoided, and gives MAS priority over later private unsecured claims.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill standardises the maximum penalty that can be awarded in all civil penalty cases to the greater of $2 million or three times the amount of benefits gained or losses avoided.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill also confers priority on MAS' civil penalty claims over private unsecured claims that accrue subsequently to the contravention of SFA.

sections.label: Asset dissipation and capital markets changes
sections.summary: This passage states the Bill reduces potential dissipation of a defendant's assets and introduces changes to capital markets legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This also reduces the potential for dissipation of a defendant's assets, which may cause MAS' civil penalty claims to be nothing more than paper judgments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: This Bill introduces significant and timely changes to our capital markets legislation, particularly to strengthen safeguards for retail investors and enhance the transparency and credibility of the securities and derivatives markets.

sections.label: Support for SFA amendment Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the extensive amendment Bill covering OTC market regulation, retail investor safeguards, benchmark transparency and enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I support this amendment Bill, which is quite extensive and probably the biggest change in a long time for SFA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It has changes, first, on the regulatory front, as the Minister mentioned, with reforms needed to strengthen regulation of the OTC markets, and now, exchanges, recommended by FSB and the Group of 20 (G20) will strengthen Singapore's financial sector hub status; second, enhancing regulatory safeguards for retail investors which is quite key; third, enhancing credibility and transparency of capital markets with new regulatory frameworks to instil better governance in the setting of financial benchmarks, such as SIBOR, and transparency in line with international best practices; and fourth, strengthening the enforcement regime against capital market misconduct and deter future offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In particular, this Bill enhances the robustness and transparency of the legal framework which could further protect the interest of investors, especially those who may not be as financially sophisticated as the bankers or financial consultants serving them.

sections.label: Retail investor safeguards and approved investor qualification
sections.summary: The passage suggests a Hong Kong-style suitability clause and notes the Bill extends safeguards and tightens approved investor qualification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: On the other hand, in Hong Kong, it will eventually be mandatory to enforce a suitability clause in all applicable client agreements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It would be a good idea to have something similar here, as this should help prevent banks from hiding behind disclaimer clauses, while enhancing the level of protection for all retail investors, including AIs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Bill enhances regulatory safeguards for retail investors by extending regulatory safeguards to retail investors in two types of non-conventional investment products that share features of capital market products such as the buy-back arrangements involving gold, silver or platinum and collectively managed investment schemes, such as land-banking.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Next, I am pleased to note that the Bill seeks to tighten the qualification to be an approved investor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: It is welcomed that the individual's primary residence can only contribute up to S$1 million of the current S$2 million net personal assets.

sections.label: EU elective professional client requirements
sections.summary: This passage sets out the European Union requirements for a retail client to become an elective professional client.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: According to the European Union laws, a retail client, in order to gain status as an "elective" professional client, must satisfy at least two of the following requirements: (a) he/she has carried out trade transactions, in significant size, at least €50,000, on the relevant market at an average frequency of 10 per quarter over the previous four quarters; (b) the size of financial instrument portfolio, defined as including cash deposits and financial instruments, exceeds €500,000; and (c) he/she works or has worked in the financial sector for at least one year in a professional position which requires knowledge of the transactions or services envisaged.

sections.label: Australia and New Zealand net asset certification
sections.summary: In Australia and New Zealand, an independent accountant must certify the client's net assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In the case of Australia and New Zealand, an independent accountant has to certify the net assets of the client.

sections.label: Impact on financial sector and implementation period
sections.summary: The passage urges examination of the amendments' impact on financial sector value-added growth and a meaningful implementation period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As a result, the impact of the amendments on the value-added growth of the financial sector should also be examined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I would also urge MAS to have a meaningful implementation period for the changes as it is very hard and expensive for the banks to get clients certified and new systems to be set up to track products.

sections.label: MAS enforcement capabilities question
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Ministry what steps are being taken to strengthen MAS and other agencies' enforcement capabilities for the widened securities and futures regulation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Given this widening of the scope of our securities and futures regulation that this Bill embodies, I would like to ask the Ministry what steps are being taken to beef up the enforcement capabilities of MAS and other agencies to proactively enforce adherence to these new rules.

sections.label: Penny stocks enforcement resources
sections.summary: The speaker cites a constituent's concern over the penny stocks incident and DPM Tharman's reply that Singapore's market misconduct investigation resources are commensurate and comparable to other developed markets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Referring to the penny stocks incident and the time it took to resolve, he was very concerned that insufficient enforcement would lead to retail investors like him losing money to rich market-movers, who may or may not be breaking the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I recently filed a Parliamentary Question on this and Deputy Prime Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam replied that the resources that Singapore has devoted to investigating market misconduct offences are commensurate with the capitalisation and number of listed companies in our securities market, and comparable with other developed markets, such as Hong Kong and Australia.

sections.label: MAS monitoring leads versus staff
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MAS monitors the ratio between incoming leads for possible breaches of the Act and the number of staff analysing those leads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, does MAS monitor the ratio between the number of incoming leads for possible breaches of the Act on the one hand, from suspicious transaction reports, electronic meta-data analysis, public feedback and so on, and the number of staff analysing those leads, on the other hand?

sections.label: Regulator and industry conflicts of interest
sections.summary: The speaker asks what steps are being taken to prevent conflicts of interest between the regulator and the industry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What steps are being taken to prevent conflicts of interest between the regulator and the industry?

sections.label: Tightened accredited investor wealth criteria
sections.summary: The Bill tightens AI wealth criteria so primary residence contributes at most S$1 million of the S$2 million net personal assets threshold, or individuals qualify with S$1 million net financial assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With the passage of this Bill, the wealth criteria for an individual to qualify as an AI will be tightened, such that the net equity of the individual's primary residence can only contribute up to S$1 million of the current S$2 million net personal assets threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Alternatively, individuals will be able to qualify as an AI if they have S$1 million of financial assets, net of any related liabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Individuals whose wealth is concentrated in their primary residence and have little liquid assets otherwise, will no longer qualify as AIs.

sections.label: Illiquid bonds in AI threshold
sections.summary: The speaker notes the S$1 million threshold presumably includes bond holdings, but some bonds may be practically illiquid, such as those of companies in debt restructuring or liquidation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, the S$1 million threshold presumably includes bond holdings, but some bonds may be illiquid in practical terms, because it is either extremely difficult or impossible to sell such bonds to the secondary markets, for example, the bonds of companies undergoing some debt restructuring exercise or companies that are undergoing liquidation.

sections.label: Retail investor threshold amendment
sections.summary: Amending the Bill would clarify conditions for retail and institutional investors, raising the retail investor threshold and safeguarding their interests.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Amending the Bill would define more clearly the conditions for retail investors and institutional investors; only part of the property value can be included as part of their personal assets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This would bring up the threshold for the retail investors and safeguard their interests.

sections.label: MAS purview over investment products
sections.summary: Once the amendments are enacted, all investment products would come under the purview of MAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Once the amendments are enacted, all investment products would come under the purview of MAS.

sections.label: MAS guidelines for SME capital
sections.summary: MAS had already issued new guidelines to improve access to new platforms, enabling SMEs and startups to raise capital more easily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Earlier on, MAS has already issued new guidelines to improve access to these new platforms, enabling SMEs and startups to raise capital more easily.

sections.label: Binary options scam reports
sections.summary: More than 30 reports of binary options scams were lodged as of 14 December, with investors losing over S$1 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Recently, there has been a sharp rise in scams involving online trading in binary options, with more than 30 reports of such scams lodged to date, as of 14 December, and investors losing more than S$1 million to unregulated binary options trading platforms.

sections.label: Short-selling disclosure and penalties
sections.summary: Clause 74 requires market participants to declare short-selling positions, and stiffer penalties apply for flouting disclosure requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: By requiring market participants to declare their short-selling positions, as prescribed in clause 74, it will go a long way to ensure responsible trading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Thirdly, I am heartened to read about the stiffer penalties for people who flout disclosure requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, will the Ministry consider imposing a two-year trading ban instead of just fines, for those who fail to meet disclosure requirements, or those who present information which gravely affects the movement of prices, thereby distorting efficient trading activities?

sections.label: LIBOR manipulation impact and punishment
sections.summary: LIBOR manipulation affected loan and savings rates worldwide, involving up to US$800 trillion in financial instruments, and MAS punished 20 banks in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Their manipulation of the LIBOR rate impacted the man-in-the-street as well as corporations around the world, because it affected what was paid for loans and earned for savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: It is estimated to involve up to US$800 trillion worth of financial instruments, ranging from complex interest rate derivatives to simple mortgages.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: In 2013, MAS punished 20 banks and revealed that 133 traders had tried to manipulate three interest rate and foreign exchange benchmarks.

sections.label: Gold buy-back losses and MAS safeguards
sections.summary: Speaker notes Singaporeans lost savings in unregulated gold buy-back arrangements and welcomes MAS extending safeguards to such debentures and CIS like land-banking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I was saddened by the heart-breaking experience of many Singaporeans, including several of my residents, who have lost their life savings in unregulated buy-back arrangements involving instruments, such as gold.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am comforted that MAS is now extending the regulatory safeguards to investors in two types of unconventional investment products.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: These include debentures involving buy-back arrangements involving gold, silver and platinum as well as CIS, such as land-banking.

sections.label: Joint accounts and regulatory burden
sections.summary: Speaker says joint account categorisation is complex, regulatory changes distract banks from clients, and asks what drives implementation priorities while urging balanced regulation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Similarly, categorisation of joint accounts as AI can be complex, with varying degrees of sophistication amongst accounts holders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, the avalanche of regulatory changes is also distracting banks from serving their clients.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: In the midst of a challenging business environment, they should instead be focusing their efforts on innovation and providing better service, enabled by smarter but not more regulation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Would the Minister please elaborate on what drives the priority of implementation of new rules?

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, we must be careful to take a balanced approach to regulation, so as not to stymie growth and impact Singapore's competitiveness.

sections.label: Amendments and financial industry challenges
sections.summary: Speaker says the amendments strengthen Singapore as a trusted financial centre, while noting wholesale banking restructuring, private banking AML regulations, and fintech disruption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The amendments put forward today strengthens our role as a trusted financial centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, echoing what my colleague Ms Foo Mee Har said, our industry is facing many challenges: (a) our wholesale banking is undergoing restructuring; (b) our private banking sector is grappling with complex regulations, especially arising from anti-money laundering requirements; and (c) our mainstream financial industry, as a whole, is being disrupted by financial technology.

sections.label: Mandating unified interest rate explanation
sections.summary: Speaker calls on MAS to mandate a simple and unified way of explaining interest rates and lending cost to protect consumers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To protect consumers, I call on MAS to mandate a simple and unified way of explaining interest rates and lending cost.

sections.label: Best formula for interest rates
sections.summary: Speaker asks MAS to share what it considers the best formula for calculating interest rates and lending cost, including fees and penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can MAS share what it considers as the best formula to calculate interest rates, be it annual percentage rate (APR), effective interest rate (EIR) or nominal rates, and lending cost, which also includes fees and penalties, to our consumers?

sections.label: CPF changes and financial literacy teaching
sections.summary: Speaker welcomes CPF changes for retirement savings and asks whether mandatory financial literacy teaching in tertiary educational institutes could be explored.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The upcoming changes to our CPF system are excellent and form an important pillar to helping Singaporeans save for retirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, I feel that now is the time for us to systematically promote financial literacy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, could we explore the mandatory teaching of financial literacy in our tertiary educational institutes?

sections.label: Financial literacy for national servicemen
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MINDEF can work with groups like MoneySENSE and SkillsFuture to teach financial literacy to young men serving the country.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, when there is time between training, can the Ministry of Defence consider working with voluntary groups like MoneySENSE to teach basic financial literacy to our young men who are sacrificing so much to serve our country?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Three, can we provide ample opportunities to attend courses on financial literacy under SkillsFuture?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (b) how could we best promote truth in lending and investing; and (c) how can we best inform our people to make sound financial decisions?

sections.label: Regulating non-conventional investment products
sections.summary: The amendment seeks to expand regulatory oversight to non-conventional investment products, which the passage calls critical.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The amendment seeks to expand the scope of regulatory oversight to non-conventional investment products and this is critical.

sections.label: Committee structure for suspicious offerings
sections.summary: The passage proposes a committee to consider suspicious offerings highlighted by the public, with issuers proving innocence and monies held in escrow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Putting these three angles together, I propose to introduce a structure whereby the committee considers suspicious offerings highlighted by the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The burden then falls on the issuer to prove that it is innocent by undergoing the full suite of regulatory due diligence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: All further activities in this issue must cease and all monies collected since must be held in escrow until regulators are satisfied.

sections.label: Classification scheme for retail investors
sections.summary: A classification scheme showing likelihood and size of capital loss and product complexity would help retail investors avoid unsuitable products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A classification scheme that indicates the likelihood of capital loss and the size of losses as well as the technical complexity of the product, would help retail investors avoid unsuitable products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In one of the consultation papers, there was mention of this complexity versus risk framework which personally I thought was a good idea.

sections.label: Scammers exploiting ignorance and information asymmetry
sections.summary: The passage states unprincipled people scam the public by exploiting ignorance and information asymmetry, and welcomes the amendment addressing this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: But that is often not what is happening.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: There are many unprincipled, immoral people whose sole expertise is to scam money from the general public, exploiting ignorance and asymmetry of information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I take great umbrage at these people for giving the finance industry a bad name.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I am pleased that this amendment takes a significant step towards addressing this scourge.

sections.label: Penalties for market misconduct offences
sections.summary: The Bill lets MAS disgorge ill-gotten benefits, claim up to three times benefits, and courts award civil penalties up to $2 million and seven years' imprisonment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Under the Bill, if the offender made substantial profits as a result of his misconduct, MAS is able to now disgorge the offender of his ill-gotten benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As MAS is able to claim a maximum penalty up to three times the benefits, this will provide a sufficiently punitive stick for his misconduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: And even if the benefits gained or losses avoided are not substantial, the Court can still award a civil penalty of up to $2 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The criminal penalty for market misconduct offences, which include the new offence of financial benchmarks manipulation in this Bill, is imprisonment of up to seven years.

sections.label: MAS opt-out for existing AI clients
sections.summary: MAS will use an opt-out approach for existing AI clients, who remain AIs if they still meet AI-eligibility criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: MAS will apply an opt-out approach for existing AI clients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, the default for existing AI clients is to remain as AIs if they continue to meet the AI-eligibility criteria.

sections.label: Startup small fund-raising exemption
sections.summary: Startups can conduct small fund-raising of up to $5 million within 12 months without issuing a prospectus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Startups can continue to conduct small fund-raising exercises of up to $5 million within 12 months without having to issue a prospectus.

sections.label: EIR for property loans and credit cards
sections.summary: For residential property loans and credit card facilities, EIR is used in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Specifically on Mr Kwek's question as to the best way to calculate interest rates, I would like to highlight that for residential property loans and credit card facilities, EIR is used in Singapore.

sections.label: Suitability obligations and void disclaimers
sections.summary: Disclaimers in client investment agreements that circumvent these obligations are void and cannot defend against mis-selling allegations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Disclaimers included in the client investment agreements that circumvent these obligations are void and cannot be used to defend against allegations of mis-selling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Financial advisers are under a legal obligation to ensure that products recommended to investors are suitable for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: For complex investment products, such as derivatives, FIs are required to assess if the investor has the relevant investment knowledge or experience before selling them to the investor.

sections.label: Central clearing for large derivatives players
sections.summary: MAS will require banks with above $20 billion notional value of OTC derivatives to centrally clear widely-traded US-dollar and Singapore-dollar interest rate derivatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Later this year, MAS will require large players, that is, banks with above $20 billion notional value of OTC derivatives, to have their widely-traded US-dollar and Singapore-dollar interest rate derivatives to be centrally cleared.

sections.label: IFL employers and participants reached
sections.summary: Since its 2012 setup, IFL has worked with more than 500 employers and organisations and reached over 100,000 participants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Since its setup in 2012, IFL has worked with more than 500 employers and organisations and reached out to over 100,000 participants.

sections.label: Binary options platforms and education
sections.summary: Some unregulated binary options platforms are on MAS' Investors Alert List, and existing programmes educate tertiary students and uniformed Servicemen, with suggestions considered as MoneySENSE is beefed up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Some of the unregulated binary options trading platforms Mr Louis Ng had mentioned are listed on MAS' Investors Alert List.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: There are existing programmes for our tertiary students and uniformed Servicemen to educate them on such matters and we will take his suggestions into account as we beef up MoneySENSE.

sections.label: Consumer empowerment and citation year
sections.summary: Consumers are empowered to take responsibility for investment decisions through disclosures and fair dealing rules supported by financial education, and the citation year changes from 2016 to 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Third, empowering consumers to take responsibility for their investment decisions through disclosures and fair dealing rules, supported by strong financial education efforts.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The citation year "2016" will be changed to "2017" as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.
